pass_a_gloss: [...] the peoples of the Saviour sanctified, clearly through the Spirit, and cleansed through the faith, he was leaping terribly and bitterly, and was making war against the Church of God, shaking against her the most unholy phalanx of the spirits under his hand; and perhaps he also thought that he could overturn her, and very much without toil, the truly venerable and holy city of God, the spiritual Jerusalem; but he was caught, having planned nothing of the things possible. For it was not possible for him to prevail, to besiege out the holy city and to overpower a right hand so most strong. For who will stand against the God who prevails in all things? So he perished together with his own shield-bearers, and was driven off from the flock of those who are godly, leaping on it in the manner of a savage beast; and he has been cast out of the tyranny against us. And this the Saviour taught us, saying: Now is judgment of this age, now the ruler of this age will be cast outside. And I, if I am lifted up on the earth, will draw all to myself. For the passion of Christ has become an overturning of death, and a pulling down of the devil, and a destruction of sin, he being lifted up on the cross, and bringing down and throwing down to earth the boast of the devil. At the right time then after those things, now too the God of all brings in the account about the birth according to flesh of the Only-Begotten, and shows beforehand the mystery through the voice of prophets, so that, the things having come out to an end, it might receive from all an undisputed belief. What then does he say? Behold indeed the Master, Lord Sabaoth, will confound the glorious with strength? Into newness of gospel life the mystery of Christ reshapes those on the earth, the more ancient customs clearly having been overturned, and the things in shadows and types no longer having the power to prevail. But this was his aim of the arrival into this world, and he has arrived to proclaim, and before the others to those from Israel, that the things laid on until a time of correction, that is, the law in letters, finally comes down to an end, the mind of those who believe being remoulded, as I said, into the better things and a spiritual way of life. For new are all the things in Christ. But although it was needed to be persuaded by him, and before the others those who preside over the synagogue of the Jews, and boast not moderately in the glories of the priesthood, they opposed from the contrary side youthfully, worked against impiously, and always speaking of the law through the all-wise Moses, they wished to show ineffective, as far as it came to them, the mystery of the economy with flesh of the Only-Begotten [the section breaks off].
pass_b_english: … peoples of the Savior, those sanctified (through the Spirit, that is) and cleansed through faith, he leapt upon terribly and bitterly. He made war on the Church of God, shaking at her the most unholy phalanx of the spirits under his hand. Perhaps he even thought he could overturn her with very little effort, the truly venerable and holy city of God, the spiritual Jerusalem. But he was caught, for none of his plans was possible. He could not besiege and take the holy city, or overpower a right hand so very strong. For who will stand against God, who can do all things?

So he perished together with his own shield-bearers, and was driven away from the flock of the godly, though he sprang on it like a savage beast; and he has been cast out of his tyranny over us. The Savior taught us this when he said: “Now is the judgment of this age; now the ruler of this age will be cast out. And I, if I am lifted up on the earth, will draw all to myself” (John 12:31–32). For the passion of Christ became the overthrow of death, the pulling down of the devil, and the destruction of sin: he was lifted up on the cross, and he brought down the devil’s boast and threw it to the ground.

In due time, then, after those events, the God of all now brings in the account of the Only-Begotten’s birth according to the flesh, and reveals the mystery beforehand through the voice of prophets, so that when the events came to fulfillment, it might be believed by all without dispute. What, then, does he say? “Behold, the Master, the Lord of Hosts, will throw the glorious into confusion with strength” (Isaiah 10:33).

The mystery of Christ refashions those on earth into the newness of gospel life (compare Romans 6:4), since the older customs are plainly overturned, and what was in shadows and types no longer has power to prevail. This was the purpose of his coming into this world. He came to proclaim, to the people of Israel before all others, that what was imposed until the time of reformation (compare Hebrews 9:10), that is, the law in letters, now at last comes to its end, as the mind of believers is remolded, as I said, into what is better and into a spiritual way of life. For all things in Christ are new (compare 2 Corinthians 5:17).

Yet though they ought to have been persuaded by him, the leaders of the synagogue of the Jews above all, who boasted not a little of the glories of the priesthood, opposed him headlong, worked against him impiously, and, though always talking of the law given through the most wise Moses, wanted to make of no effect, as far as it lay with them, the mystery of the Only-Begotten’s economy in the flesh …

choices.english: shaking at her the most unholy phalanx
choices.why: The devil shakes his host of spirits at the Church; the Church is not the one besieging.
rejected: the Church was besieged by the phalanx

choices.english: he was caught, for none of his plans was possible
choices.why: ἁλίσκομαι with the participle: he was caught out, having planned nothing that could be done.
rejected: he was foolish and did not understand anything

choices.why: νοητός set against the earthly city; 'spiritual' is the plain reader's word.
The simile describes the devil springing on the flock.
οἰκονομία is the technical word for the Incarnation and its saving plan; kept as 'economy'.
